title: Imperfect Public Monitoring with Costly Punishment: An Experimental Study

original_source.version_note: Pre-publication author manuscript matching title/authors and central contribution; exact final wording may differ.

central_claims: Under imperfect monitoring standard punishment reduces net public-good-game earnings; severe punishment offsets costs with cooperation, producing a U-shaped payoff relation.

source_manifest.title: Imperfect Public Monitoring with Costly Punishment: An Experimental Study
source_manifest.finding: Original central claims were recorded before follow-up grading.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics — Supplement, Tables S1–S2
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent comparison tests whether regular punishment under imperfect monitoring reduces net earnings; replication N=357, original focal N=117, p=.012. The project only retested one selected result per paper.

answers.rationale: The independent preregistered replication supported the focal result that regular punishment under imperfect monitoring reduces net earnings (p=.012, N=357). This judgment is restricted to that central component; it does not validate all other claims.
